---
name: digest
description: Write a prose digest of logged ingests and evergreen changes for a completed calendar period.
argument-hint: "[day|week|month]"
disable-model-invocation: true
---

Resolve the vault per [`references/vault.md`](../../references/vault.md).

## Window

Use the last completed calendar `day`, `week` (Monday–Sunday), or `month` in local time; ask if the argument is empty. Select log timestamps from midnight on the first date up to, excluding, midnight after the last.

Return an existing digest for the same period unchanged; match its period metadata, or explicit coverage in older digests.

## Synthesize

1. Read the **log** for ingests and evergreen changes in range, then pull their **source summaries** and **evergreen pages**. Base the synthesis on those logged changes.
2. Write one prose synthesis into **digests**, grouped by domain tag. Title it for its throughline and record the window in the constitution's digest-period fields. Choose another title if its filename is occupied.

Done when an existing digest is returned unchanged, or all selected material is synthesized into one digest with its period recorded and every claim linked to its page.

---
name: ingest
description: Ingest a source into the wiki — fetch a URL or video, or sweep the raw inbox, then preserve the raw source, write its source summary, and fold it into every page it touches.
argument-hint: "[source]"
disable-model-invocation: true
---

Ingest a source into the wiki — preserve the raw source, write its source summary, and fold it into every page it touches.

Resolve the vault per [`references/vault.md`](../../references/vault.md).

Match raw sources and source summaries by source URL or raw-source link. Reuse existing paths for the same source; otherwise choose an unused filename.

## Get the raw source

Start from whichever entry point you were invoked with:

- **A source given** — a URL in the argument. Fetch the full text and save it verbatim in the **raw inbox**; if unavailable, report that and stop. Interactive by default: read it, talk the takeaways over with the user, then file.
  - **A video URL** — YouTube, Vimeo, TED, or any other site yt-dlp supports: its full text is the transcript. Run [`scripts/fetch_transcript.sh`](scripts/fetch_transcript.sh) `<url>`; its header documents the output. Exit 4: rerun with the known spoken language as argument 2; ask the user if unknown. Any other failure: report the script's error output and stop.
- **No argument** — sweep the **raw inbox** for every raw source the constitution defines as **unprocessed**, including previously processed ones that have changed. Batch them with less back-and-forth.

## File it

For each raw source:

1. Write or update one page in **source summaries** that preserves the source's arguments, evidence, and caveats.
2. Fold the source into every **evergreen page** it touches — the concepts it informs and the entities it names, often many. Update every matching evergreen page; link the rest as **candidates**, using their intended evergreen paths when names collide.
3. After steps 1–2 succeed, set or refresh the raw source's processed stamp so the next sweep skips it. Never edit the raw source beyond the stamp.

Done when every raw source has a source summary and every concept or entity it touches has either an updated evergreen page or a candidate link to its intended evergreen path.

---
name: lint-wiki
description: Health-check the whole wiki — contradictions, stale claims, orphans, gaps — plus where it should grow next, with candidate pages for the user to pick. Report, auto-fix the safe ones, write the picks.
disable-model-invocation: true
---

Health-check the whole wiki: sweep every page for what's broken or missing, report it, fix the safe ones in place, and write the candidate pages the user picks. Run it periodically as the wiki grows.

Resolve the vault per [`references/vault.md`](../../references/vault.md).

## Checks

Run every check across the wiki — a full sweep, not a spot-check. Add any the constitution defines on top of these.

- **Contradictions** — incompatible claims presented as current in the same context. Preserve attributed source disagreements.
- **Stale claims** — outdated assertions still presented as current.
- **Stale pages** — evergreen pages with time-sensitive information due for review. Explain what needs rechecking and why.
- **Orphans** — evergreen pages with no inbound links from outside the **index** and **log**.
- **Duplicates** — two pages for one concept or entity.
- **Missing cross-references** — pages that should link to each other and don't.
- **Unlisted tags** — a tag the constitution's tag list leaves out, on a page the constitution says to tag: an agent's slip, or a tag the user added by hand. Report each with the pages that carry it; the user approves it onto the list or has it replaced.
- **Missing aliases** — an acronym or alternate name used for an existing page but absent from its alias metadata.
- **Broken links** — missing or incorrect link targets, except candidates.
- **Data gaps** — a question the wiki raises but never answers, fillable with a web search.
- **Unprocessed raw sources** — raw sources in the **raw inbox** that the constitution defines as unprocessed. The fix is `/memex-skills:ingest` with no argument, which processes them all.

Then the generative half — where the wiki should grow next:

- **Candidates** — concepts and entities without a matching **evergreen page**, found in unresolved links, recurring unlinked names, or mentions linked to another role.
- **New questions** worth investigating from what's already here.
- **New sources** worth hunting down to fill the thin spots.

## Report and fix

Report every finding. Auto-fix only the safe, mechanical ones — a missing cross-reference, a missing alias, or a broken link with an unambiguous existing target. Repair link destinations as well as alias metadata: target the actual filename, qualify its path when names collide, and preserve the display text (`[[Page Name|Alias]]`). Leave ambiguous targets and judgment calls — contradictions, stale claims, what to reconcile — for the user to rule on.

Qualify candidate links whose names collide so they remain unresolved. Report the candidates as a pick list, ranked by how many pages mention each, with those pages as its evidence. Write the ones the user picks as **evergreen pages** from the pages that mention them, and link their mentions to the chosen pages; the rest stay candidates.

Done when every check has run across the wiki, each finding is either fixed or reported, and every candidate the user picked has an evergreen page with its mentions linked to it.

# Memex Skills Skills for an [LLM Wiki](https://gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f), Andrej Karpathy's pattern for a personal knowledge base that an agent maintains. You collect sources and ask questions; the agent summarizes, cross-links, and keeps the wiki consistent as it grows. There are three skills: [`/ingest`](#1-ingest) files and summarizes sources; [`/digest`](#2-digest) connects what you learned over a day, week, or month; and [`/lint-wiki`](#3-lint-wiki) finds problems in your wiki, fixes them, and suggests new pages. They follow your vault's **constitution** (`AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`), so the folder names and page formats stay yours. Like [Agency Skills](../agency-skills), they are human-invocable only: they add nothing to your model's system prompt, and agents cannot invoke them implicitly. ## The Pattern Karpathy's gist describes three architectural layers and leaves the implementation to you: | Layer | What it holds | Who writes it | | --- | --- | --- | | Raw sources | Preserved full-text originals saved locally, available when their URLs stop working | You and the agent | | Generated wiki | Knowledge the agent compiles from those sources and maintains as it grows, plus an index and activity log | The agent; you pick new evergreen pages | | Schema | Your vault's constitution: folder mappings, frontmatter, tags, page formats, and workflows | You and the agent | The generated wiki contains three kinds of content: - **Source summaries** — one page per ingested article, paper, or video, preserving its author's arguments, evidence, and caveats. The length fits the source: a short announcement may need a paragraph; a paper may warrant detailed notes. - **Evergreen pages** — concept and entity pages that connect what you learn across sources and evolve as your understanding changes. - **Digests** — reviews of logged ingests and evergreen changes for a completed calendar period. Raw sources protect against link rot. Source summaries make individual sources easy to revisit; evergreen pages bring their contributions together while keeping each author's claims attributed. The **constitution** maps each content role to a folder, so the paths stay yours. The [template](AGENTS.example.md) uses `Sources/` as the raw inbox for raw sources, `Wiki/` for concept and entity pages, `Wiki/Summaries/` for source summaries, and `Wiki/Digests/` for digests. ## Installation Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode install Memex Skills as a plugin. Other harnesses install its skills through the [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills).
Claude Code Run from your terminal: ```bash claude plugin install memex-skills --marketplace jehudarajasa/skills ```
Codex ```bash codex plugin marketplace add jehudarajasa/skills codex plugin add memex-skills@jehudarajasa ```
OpenCode ```bash opencode plugin --global @jehudarajasa/memex-skills ```
Other Harnesses ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/jehudarajasa/skills/tree/skills-dist/plugins/memex-skills --global --agent cursor --skill '*' ``` Replace `cursor` with your agent's name.
Video ingest requires [`yt-dlp`](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp) and [`jq`](https://jqlang.org) on your `PATH`, plus captions in the video's spoken language. ## Setup Copy [`AGENTS.example.md`](AGENTS.example.md) to your vault's root as `AGENTS.md`, then follow the comment at its top: rename the folders to yours, seed your tags, add a `CLAUDE.md` that imports it, and create an empty `index.md` and `log.md`. Or let your agent do it: give it the template's link and your vault's path, and ask it to follow the comment. It can map folders you already have onto the roles. Already have notes in the vault? Folders not listed in the constitution stay yours: the agent reads them when relevant and edits them only when you ask. ## Skills Run the skills from inside your vault. ### 1. [`/ingest`](skills/ingest/SKILL.md) File a source into the wiki. Give it the URL of an article, paper, or video: it saves the full text as a raw source in the raw inbox, talks the takeaways over with you, and writes the source summary. Run it with no argument to process every raw source your constitution defines as unprocessed. Either way, it updates every evergreen page the source touches and links the missing ones as [candidates](#why-new-pages-are-your-pick). ``` /memex-skills:ingest https://gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f /memex-skills:ingest ``` ### 2. [`/digest`](skills/digest/SKILL.md) Review logged ingests and evergreen changes for the last completed day, week, or month with claims linked to their pages. Reruns return the existing digest unchanged. ``` /memex-skills:digest week ``` ### 3. [`/lint-wiki`](skills/lint-wiki/SKILL.md) Health-check the whole wiki: contradictions, stale claims and pages, orphans, duplicates, missing links and aliases, and unprocessed raw sources. It fixes the mechanical problems, reports the rest for you to rule on, and suggests where the wiki should grow next. That includes the candidate pages, ranked by how many pages mention them, for you to pick. ## Rationales ### Why New Pages Are Your Pick Karpathy's version lets the agent create pages freely, and it will create a page for every concept and entity a source mentions, whether you need one or not. Ingest a few articles on Ralph loops and you get a Claude Code page too, though you already know what Claude Code is. Pages like that bloat the wiki. They bury the pages you do need, and every later ingest and lint has one more page to keep current. So `/ingest` writes the source summary and updates the evergreen pages that already exist, but it creates none. A concept or entity without a page stays an unresolved `[[link]]`: a **candidate**. `/lint-wiki` lists the candidates, ranked by how many pages mention them, and writes only the ones you pick. Obsidian already shows unresolved links, so candidates need no extra file, and the ones you skip keep collecting mentions until they earn a page. ## License [MIT](../../LICENSE)

# LLM Wiki

This Obsidian vault is an **LLM Wiki** (Karpathy pattern): the human captures, the agent ingests and maintains. Obsidian is the IDE, you (the agent) are the programmer, this wiki is the codebase.

## Orient First (Every Session)

1. Read `index.md`.
2. Read the last entries of `log.md` — recent activity.

After changing the vault, update `index.md` (if pages changed) and append to `log.md`.

## Architecture and Roles

The architectural layers are **raw sources**, the **generated wiki**, and the **schema** (this `AGENTS.md`). Source summaries, evergreen pages, and digests are content within the generated wiki.

| Layer | Folder | Owner | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Raw sources | `Sources/` | Shared | **Raw inbox** — immutable Markdown raw sources: full text the human captures (Web Clipper output) or the agent saves. The link-rot backstop and the feedstock for ingest. |
| Generated wiki | `Wiki/Summaries/` | Agent | **Source summaries** — one self-contained page per ingested article, paper, or video, preserving its arguments, evidence, and caveats. Update it when the raw source changes. |
| Generated wiki | `Wiki/` | Agent | **Evergreen pages** — cross-linked concept and entity pages. The compounding knowledge. |
| Generated wiki | `Wiki/Digests/` | Agent | **Digests** — one synthesis per completed calendar period. |

The **index** (`index.md`, the page catalog) and the **log** (`log.md`, the audit trail) live at the vault root beside this file. Folders not listed above hold the human's own notes: read them when relevant, and edit them only when the human asks.

## Frontmatter

Every generated page in `Wiki/`, including `Wiki/Summaries/` and `Wiki/Digests/`, uses these common fields:

```yaml
---
title: <page title>
type: source | concept | entity | digest
summary: <one line — shown in the index>
aliases: [] # acronyms & alternate names for discovery
created: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS±HH:MM
updated: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS±HH:MM
tags: [] # hierarchical domain tags — see Tags below
---
```

Combine the common fields with the matching page-type block:

**Source summaries**

```yaml
type: source
source_url: <URL>
source_type: article | paper | video
author: <the writer; for a video, the channel>
published: YYYY-MM-DD # source's publication date, when known
raw: "[[Sources/<raw filename>]]"
```

**Concepts**

```yaml
type: concept
```

**Entities**

```yaml
type: entity
```

**Digests**

```yaml
type: digest
period_start: YYYY-MM-DD # inclusive local start date
period_end: YYYY-MM-DD # inclusive local end date
```

Raw sources in `Sources/` stay as captured. After successfully ingesting one, set or refresh its `processed: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS±HH:MM` stamp. The stamp is the only raw source content the agent may edit. A modified raw source or one with no stamp is **unprocessed**.

## Tags

Tag every generated page in `Wiki/` with one or more hierarchical domain tags (`ai`, `ai/agent`) from the list below; they group the digests and `index.md`. The human approves every new tag: when no listed tag fits, tag the page `misc` and propose a new tag or subtag to the human, then add it to the list once they approve.

**Domain tags:**

- `misc` — pages no listed tag fits yet

## Evergreen Pages

- **Concept** (`type: concept`) — an idea, technique, term, or principle (RAG, Compound Interest). Extend one whenever an idea recurs or is clearly durable; prefer extending an existing page over creating a near-duplicate.
- **Entity** (`type: entity`) — a named person, org, product, place, or event (Andrej Karpathy, Obsidian). Entities link to the concepts they exemplify; concepts link to key entities.

A new concept or entity page is the human's pick. Until a matching evergreen page exists, link its intended path as an unresolved **candidate**, even if a raw source or human note has the same name. `lint-wiki` offers it, ranked by how many pages mention it.

## Page Shape

### Concept & Entity Pages

```
## Summary       — 1–3 sentences, the gist
## <body>        — sections as needed
## Sources       — [[links]] to Wiki/Summaries/ pages + external URLs
## Related       — [[links]] to sibling pages
```

Small pages may be just Summary + Sources. Link liberally with `[[Page Name]]` — associative trails are the whole point.

### Source Summaries

Start at `## Summary`; the title lives in the frontmatter. Match the detail to the source: a short announcement may need only a paragraph; a substantial paper may need detailed notes on its arguments, evidence, and caveats.

```
## Summary  — the source's main claim and takeaways
## Notes    — arguments, evidence, and caveats that need elaboration, when useful
## Quotes   — 0–2 verbatim lines, each with speaker and locator
```

- **Summary** — grounded in the raw source; the first sentence states the source's main claim.
- **Notes** — expand on the Summary when the source warrants it. Each bold line is a claim the source makes. End each support bullet with a locator — `[mm:ss]` for a video, `§Section` for an article, `p. N` for a paper. Bold the top-level lines only. Reach for a table or Mermaid diagram where the structure is visual (a comparison, a flow).
- **Quotes** — copied from the raw source, so each one checks against it. Omit the section when nothing is quotable.

Link concepts and entities inline in the Summary and Notes as `[[links]]`: these claims are what ingest folds into evergreen pages. Name who holds each opinion or forecast.

## Answering Questions

Answer from the wiki's pages, cited as `[[links]]`. When an answer has lasting value — a comparison, an analysis, a connection you discovered — offer to **file it back** as a new `Wiki/` page; it may be a page, a table, or a Marp deck.

## Conventions

- Propose a split for approval when a concept page covers distinct concepts.
- Concept titles: Title Case, singular. Preserve source titles and entities' proper names.
- Link existing pages by their actual filenames (`[[Page Name]]`); use `[[Page Name|Alias]]` to display an acronym or alternate name.
- When filenames collide, qualify the intended role's path, including candidate links: `[[Wiki/Vannevar Bush|Vannevar Bush]]` targets the evergreen page, even while only `Sources/Vannevar Bush.md` exists.
- Absolute timestamps — ISO 8601 with the local timezone offset (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS±HH:MM`; `date -Iseconds` prints one), never "today".
- `log.md` entries: one plain paragraph each, `[YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS±HH:MM] <op> | <summary>` — keep them grep-able (`grep "^\[" log.md`).
- `index.md` is the catalog _you_ maintain and read first: one line per generated page in `Wiki/`, including source summaries and digests, `- [[<page path>]] — <summary>`, under the heading of its first domain tag's top-level tag (`ai/agent` sits under `` ## AI `#ai` ``). One heading per top-level tag in use; within each, evergreen pages first, then source summaries, then digests.

# Resolving the vault

Every wiki skill runs against a **vault** — an LLM Wiki (Karpathy pattern) whose root `AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`) is the **constitution**. Resolve the vault the same way every run, read the constitution, and run the operation in the vault's own terms.

## Which vault

From the working directory upward, use the nearest directory whose `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` declares the LLM Wiki pattern. If none matches, ask the user for the vault path.

## The constitution binds the specifics

The skills speak in **roles**; the constitution binds each role to this vault's concrete paths, frontmatter, and page shape. Match roles by purpose, using only the paths and field names the constitution defines. The roles a skill may name:

- **raw inbox** — holds immutable **raw sources**, the link-rot backstop and the feedstock ingest sweeps.
- **source summaries** — one self-contained page per ingested source, preserving its arguments, evidence, and caveats for convenient review.
- **evergreen pages** — the cross-linked concept and entity pages, the compounding knowledge. New ones are the user's pick: a concept or entity without a matching evergreen page stays an unresolved `[[link]]` — a **candidate** — until the user picks it in `lint-wiki`, even if a raw source, source summary, digest, or human note has the same name.
- **digests** — dated snapshots of a window (day/week/month). Preserve their wording and claims; allow only mechanical link and metadata repairs that preserve meaning.
- **index** and **log** — the map the agent maintains, and the audit trail it appends.

Resolve links by the intended page's role as well as its name. For name collisions, use the intended page's vault-relative path, including the future evergreen path for candidates, and preserve the display name with `[[path/to/Page|Page]]`.

The constitution also owns the **session-close protocol** — what to update and append when an operation ends. Follow it; the skill body carries only its own operation.

## Access

A vault outside the working directory may not be readable until the user grants access. If a read or write is denied or prompts, that's the signal: ask the user to grant it — in-session `/add-dir "<vault>"`, permanently via `permissions.additionalDirectories`, or by approving the prompt. If the constitution itself is unreadable, stop and say so; the vault is the source of truth, so build nothing to stand in for it.
